traits.native_range: underwater — Fucus vesiculosus, North Atlantic intertidal rock, olive-brown rockweed with air bladders 30-100 cm — Wikip
traits.leaf_shape: strap or rosette leaves in a clump on a branch
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: brown alga: flat dichotomous fronds with a midrib and paired air bladders, drawn as straps

bark.note: holdfast and short stipe; no stem surface

growth.juvenile_note: No juvenile form to draw: zygotes stick to rock and within weeks become tiny flat germlings anchored by a disc; the young frond is a small, flat, forked olive blade with a midrib that gains paired air bladders as it grows. Mature plants are 30-100 cm leathery forked fronds with paired bladders and swollen, warty fruiting tips.
growth.source: MarLIN species account (Fucus vesiculosus: germlings visible in ~2 weeks; growth 0.3-0.8 cm/week in summer; lifespan 2-5 yr; receptacles form in winter, gametes mid-winter to late summer); Wikipedia (fronds to 150 x 2.5 cm with midrib and paired vesicles; sheltered mid-lower shores).

ground.name: Feather boa kelp
ground.source: underwater — Egregia menziesii, Pacific coast Alaska-Baja, low intertidal rock, strap-like fronds 2-8 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Egregia menziesii, Pacific coast Alaska-Baja, low intertidal rock, strap-like fronds 2-8 m — Wikipedia
traits.trunk: long woody or soft climbing stem on a host
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: brown alga: long flattened rachis fringed with small blades and floats

bark.note: holdfast and short stipe; no stem surface

growth.juvenile_note: Spores grow into microscopic gametophytes; the young sporophyte appears as a small, simple, flat brown blade with a wavy edge on a tiny holdfast. It then elongates into the adult form: long, flat, strap-like rachises fringed along both edges with many small blades and olive-shaped gas floats, several straps rising from one branched holdfast and trailing like a feather boa.
growth.source: Wikipedia Egregia (fronds may exceed 5 m; flat strap-like rachis, smooth or corrugated, lined with small blades a few cm long and pneumatocysts). Kelp life cycle (microscopic gametophytes), growth rate, maturity and lifespan estimated from laminarian kelp literature.

fruiting.source: A kelp has no flowers or fruit: values map its sporophylls, small smooth fertile blades clustered on the lower rachis whose sori shed spores into the water (spring-autumn), then erode away; torn fronds cast ashore rot in weeks. All timings and counts estimated from laminarian kelp biology.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two narrow strap-like cotyledons, then a small rosette of fleshy grey-green leaves divided into narrow, cylindrical, pointed segments. It wedges its root into rock crevices or shingle, becomes woody at the base and builds a low, rounded, succulent-leaved clump that carries flat umbels of greenish-yellow flowers from its second summer.
growth.source: PFAF (0.3 x 0.3 m, fast; flowers Jun-Aug, seed ripe Aug-Oct; germinates in 3-6 weeks at 15 C; no shade); Wikipedia Crithmum (to 50 cm, woody base, fleshy lobed leaves, greenish-yellow umbels); RHS; age at first flowering and lifespan estimated

ground.name: Sea fig
ground.source: Carpobrotus chilensis (C. edulis similar), Pacific coast bluffs Chile/California (S Africa origin for edulis), succulent mats 5-20 cm — Wikipedia

traits.leaf_shape: tiny leaves packed in a dome
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: trailing succulent stems, green becoming reddish and woody

growth.juvenile_note: Two plump succulent cotyledons, then opposite pairs of fleshy three-angled finger-like leaves, a miniature of the adult. The seedling soon lies down and sends trailing stems across sand or bluffs, rooting at some nodes, becoming a low spreading mat of green to red-tinged succulent leaves with magenta daisy-like flowers.
growth.source: Cal-IPC plant assessment for C. chilensis (stems grow several feet a year once established; less branched and rooted than C. edulis; ~3-fold cover increase over 25 yr at one site); Vila & D'Antonio 1998 (Carpobrotus germination and growth); timings estimated from C. edulis

ground.name: Sea lettuce
ground.source: underwater — Ulva lactuca, worldwide intertidal rock and pools, thin bright-green sheets 10-30 cm — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Ulva lactuca, worldwide intertidal rock and pools, thin bright-green sheets 10-30 cm — Wikipedia
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: green alga: thin translucent bright green sheets

growth.juvenile_note: Settled swimming spores or zygotes (microscopic) grow into a short green filament, then a tiny tube or cushion that splits open into a flat blade only two cells thick on a minute disc holdfast. It shows as a bright green fleck after 1-2 weeks and expands in a few weeks into a crinkled, translucent, lettuce-like sheet; fertile margins turn olive-yellow, release spores and then fall apart.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Ulva lactuca): sheet to 18 cm or more long and up to 30 cm across, on rocks and other algae in the littoral and sublittoral worldwide; diploid and haploid plants look alike, alternating via zoospores and gametes; eaten in soups and salads. Settlement-to-visible, growth and fertility timings estimated from the genus (fast-growing, fertile within weeks, repeated summer spore releases).

ground.silhouette: tight green cushion with pink heads

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two small oval cotyledons, then narrow, grass-like dark green leaves in a tiny rosette on a stout taproot. Rosettes multiply as the woody base branches, building a dense, rounded cushion of hundreds of linear leaves; from about year 2, leafless stalks 5-30 cm tall carry round pink papery pompom heads.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Armeria maritima: compact evergreen perennial in low clumps with long flower stems and globes of bright pink flowers; flowers Apr-Oct in British salt marshes; bee and butterfly pollinated; sea cliffs, dunes, salt marsh; copper tolerant). Germination, cushion growth, first flowering and lifespan estimated from Woodell & Dale 1993 as recalled.

shrub.name: Coastal rosemary
shrub.source: Westringia fruticosa, New South Wales sea cliffs and headlands, grey-leaved rounded shrub 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: Westringia fruticosa, New South Wales sea cliffs and headlands, grey-leaved rounded shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: The seedling is one upright stem with narrow, grey-green, rosemary-like leaves in whorls of four, felted white underneath with rolled-under edges. It branches freely from low down, so by its second year it is already a dense, rounded, grey-green bun of stiff leafy stems that flowers while still small.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Westringia fruticosa): coastal New South Wales shrub with white, hairy, two-lipped flowers spotted orange to purple, flowering all year. Size and fast growth from horticultural descriptions; germination (usually grown from cuttings), first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (Westringia fruticosa, Westringia): white hairy flowers with a two-lobed upper lip and orange-to-purple spots, two fertile stamens, flowering all year. Flower size, fruit (four tiny nutlets held in the calyx), pollinators, timings and crop estimated from the genus and the mint family.

traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: thick grey-brown fibrous bark in vertical strips

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: 3-5 needle-like cotyledons, then whorls of soft, spreading, blue-green needle-like juvenile leaves for the first year or so before the tight, rope-like scale leaves take over. Young trees are dense, narrow bright-green cones or columns with branches to the ground; the flat-topped, wind-sculpted crowns of the headlands come only after decades.
growth.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (Cupressus: C. macrocarpa pollinated in March, cones ripen 15-18 months later, cone crops usually begin before age 10, ~140 seeds/cone, 35-day germination tests, epigeal). Growth rate (fast when young) and longevity (the Lone Cypress is thought to be ~250 yr) estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (Cupressus: pollination March, woody cones up to 3 cm ripen 15-18 months after pollination, open when ripe, abundant cone crops); empty cones persist on branches for years (hang and rot times, crop and set estimated).
